items.explanation: Stacks results and removes duplicate rows. Column counts and types must match.
items.example: SELECT country FROM customers UNION SELECT country FROM suppliers ORDER BY country;
items.expected: Every country of a customer or supplier, once.

items.example: SELECT 'customer' AS type, city FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT 'supplier', city FROM suppliers LIMIT 10;

items.explanation: Distinct rows present in both results.
items.example: SELECT country FROM customers INTERSECT SELECT country FROM suppliers ORDER BY country;
items.expected: Countries with both customers and suppliers.

items.explanation: Distinct rows of the first result not in the second (Oracle: MINUS).
items.example: SELECT country FROM customers EXCEPT SELECT country FROM suppliers ORDER BY country;

items.syntax: SELECT id FROM a EXCEPT SELECT id FROM b
items.explanation: Anti-join on whole rows; treats NULLs as equal.
items.example: SELECT product_id FROM products EXCEPT SELECT product_id FROM order_details ORDER BY product_id;

items.explanation: ORDER BY and LIMIT after the last query apply to the whole result.
items.example: SELECT company_name FROM customers UNION SELECT company_name FROM suppliers ORDER BY company_name LIMIT 5;

items.syntax: WITH all AS (… UNION ALL …) SELECT type, COUNT(*) …
items.explanation: UNION ALL then GROUP BY to summarise several tables.
items.example: WITH e AS (SELECT 'customer' AS type, country FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT 'supplier', country FROM suppliers) SELECT type, COUNT(*) FROM e GROUP BY type;
